answer: An agent economy can make each new identity earn its place by completing a fresh, randomly assigned piece of verifiable useful work — checking a data batch or computing a proof — before activation. The task is drawn unpredictably, like a raven picking one twig from a glacier of possibilities, bound to the applicant's key and useless to anyone else. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must do a thousand distinct jobs, each checked at the harbor where work enters the ledger, so a Sybil army costs as much as real labor while honest agents pay only once.
